subject.title: Feature Request: Add parseMode config for Telegram channels

question: Should Telegram expose a forced-plain account setting, and should its public contract be limited to safe `auto | plain` behavior rather than Telegram API parse-mode dialects?
rationale: Current delivery intentionally renders through OpenClaw-owned formatting and escaping. Source evidence cannot safely choose new raw-markup semantics, inheritance behavior, or defaults without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add safe auto/plain mode
options.body: Expose an account-inheritable `auto | plain` setting that preserves current behavior by default while allowing unformatted delivery without raw-markup semantics.

options.title: Keep automatic formatting
options.body: Retain standard formatted delivery, plain fallback on formatting failure, and the existing rich-message switch without adding another setting.

options.title: Expose Telegram dialects
options.body: Support Telegram-specific Markdown or HTML values only after defining trusted-content, escaping, fallback, and upgrade contracts for every delivery path.

recommendation.title: Add safe auto/plain mode
recommendation.body: Expose an account-inheritable `auto | plain` setting that preserves current behavior by default while allowing unformatted delivery without raw-markup semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history and issue-discussion signals connect this person to the original formatting transition and subsequent Telegram configuration review.
